items.note: Children do a standardized drawing task with a social robot that gives either contextualized feedback from a vision-language model or pre-recorded generic compliments; creative product value is scored. N=49 is below 50, and the comparison arm is not generative AI, so the next stage should check whether it counts as a different AI configuration.

Lab experiment where participants brainstorm alone or with GenAI assistance, crossed with anticipating a human or AI teammate; idea quantity, quality, originality, and flexibility are scored. Abstract does not state random assignment.

Meta-analysis of 17 studies (115 effect sizes) comparing human ideas with GenAI-prompted ideas; small non-significant pooled effect favoring GenAI. PsyArXiv preprint and MIC 2025 abstract are versions of the same work.

Systematic review and three-level meta-analysis of 19 studies (61 effect sizes) on homogenization in human-AI co-creation; small significant homogenization effect. Same work as the ECCE 2026 short paper and the PsyArXiv preprint; its study list is a source for candidates.

Analyzes over six million text-to-image prompts on CivitAI over seven months and finds prompt language homogenizes as participation grows, with lexical similarity tied to lower visual diversity (Vendi scores).

Preregistered BCG experiment randomly assigning 758 consultants to no AI, GPT-4, or GPT-4 with a prompt overview on 18 creative-to-analytical tasks; quality is scored. Same study as SSRN 4573321 (HBS WP 24-013), whose text reports reduced variability of AI users' ideas; the abstract does not mention diversity.

Preregistered field experiment at Procter & Gamble randomly assigning 791 professionals to AI or no AI, alone or in pairs, on real product innovation challenges; solution quality is scored. NBER WP 33641 reports N=776 for the same study.

Within-subject study (N=37) of conceptual ideation with an unmodified LLM, a concept-suppressed LLM, and unaided; reported quantitative outcomes are workload and perceived ownership (self-reports), so it is unclear whether ideas are scored. Below 50 participants.

Preregistered metaphor-writing experiment with native and non-native English writers in three arms (no AI, AI ideation, AI refinement); collective diversity and individual ratings are scored, and LLM persona simulations are added. Abstract does not state N or assignment method.

At BSH, ideas from ChatGPT are compared with ideas from an expert workshop on sustainable packaging, rated for novelty, value, and feasibility, plus a qualitative part. Holzner et al. 2025 also code it as people with vs without AI, so the next stage may check whether any experts worked with AI.
